limitations: Canvas rendering (snake movement, food pixels, collisions) cannot be observed via DOM assertions; game-over screen and score changes from eating food are not directly testable.
Game-over screen requires driving the snake into a wall, which depends on time-based ticks and canvas state and is not reachable through deterministic DOM-only checks.
Arrow-key movement effects are only observable on the canvas; only the paused-state no-op behavior is checked.
Synthetic key events may not exactly mirror trusted browser keyboard input.
Score value after eating food depends on random food placement and timing, so it cannot be predicted.
Space key pause/resume relies on keydown listener; only the pause direction is checked, resume via space is not.

# Pixel Snake

A self-contained offline browser game built with plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No packages, network requests, or external assets required.

## How to Play

- Use the **arrow keys** (or **WASD**) to move the snake.
- Eat the red pixel to grow and increase your score.
- Avoid hitting the walls or your own tail.
- The game starts paused with instructions on screen.

## Controls

| Action | Key / Button |
|--------|--------------|
| Move | Arrow keys / WASD |
| Pause / Resume | Space or P, or the Pause button |
| Restart | R, or the Restart button |

## Running Locally

Open `index.html` in any modern browser. No server or build step needed.

## File Overview

- `index.html` — page structure and controls
- `style.css` — responsive card layout and palette
- `game.js` — game loop, input handling, and canvas rendering
